original.concept: The per-card engage flask on the crafting table — the light that lifts the flask off its own backplate, so the button reads as a lit object sitting on the disc rather than a sticker printed on it.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (combination_screen merge fabs): a tight pale halo hugging the flask art's own alpha (texture-sourced `glow` RenderFilter, same path as the map's forge flask), slim spread with a near-linear falloff so it stays dense right up to the edge instead of dissolving. Deliberately STEADY, not breathing: one of these rides every valid partner card at once, and a gridful of pulsing halos reads as noise rather than as an invitation.

original.concept: The gold a slain enemy pays, made countable: one coin per gold arcing off the corpse and into the run's purse on the left rail.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (CoinFlightFx): one coin per gold, all riding the same path from the corpse to the gold bag — a CIRCLE ARC, so both halves of the flight are the same shape mirrored and the coin holds one speed from corpse to bag (constant curvature = constant speed, at no cost). THE RULE: a coin never moves away from the bag, on either axis, by a single pixel. `curve` is the one dial: 0 = the straight diagonal, 1 = the roundest arc the two points allow — a true quarter-circle when the horizontal and vertical distances are equal, flattening toward straight as they stop being, and dead straight when the corpse and the bag share a Y (bending there would carry the coin back past the bag). The ceiling is one angle, not a clamp, so there is nothing to correct at any distance. Coins are staggered by `stagger` and separated by varying the dial itself (`spread`), never by offsetting the path in pixels — an offset would push a coin outside the box.
original.prompt: Sprite sheet of a spinning gold coin with a bright specular sweep, transparent background, 8 frames, 2d game effect

original.concept: The reward leaving the opened chest and carrying itself to the middle of the screen — the physical link between winning the fight and the rewards screen, so the two are one motion and not a cut.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (RewardOrbFx): a bright orb gathers over the open lid, eases out of it ALONG the flight line (never upward — the chest sits in the enemy king's slot at the TOP of the board, so an upward lift plus a downward flight read as a bounce off the ceiling), then travels unhurried in a STRAIGHT line to the viewport centre trailing sparks (arc>0 bows that path); on arrival it throws a ring and fires the caller's on_arrive (which is what lets Combat navigate). Drawn on the VFX overlay so it outlives combat and lingers over the screen growing out from under it.

original.concept: A screen arriving as the TAIL of a gesture rather than a jump — it swells from nothing at the centre of the viewport, so whatever the player just did appears to have opened it.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (ScreenGrowFx, registered app-wide in VfxService): the mounted content holds hidden for `delay`, then scales 0 → 1 about the viewport centre with a slight overshoot and fades in. The hold is what makes it read as coming OUT of the cue that summoned it (the reward orb's burst) rather than detonating alongside it — tune it against reward_orb's `burst`. Requested per navigation via Nav.goto(path, "screen_grow_in"); every other navigation keeps the standard sweep. The persistent chrome is not scaled — it belongs to the Shell, not the arriving screen.

original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (combat_board attack preview): a composited GlowFx — reads the target CardUI's TRUE silhouette (card + all badges/pips) and radiates on the overlay layer, so it never clips and never covers a badge; attached while a friendly unit is selected or dragged, paired with the red crosshair slot marker.

original.concept: THE canonical 'this is selected / active' treatment for any widget, anywhere — one visual language for selection (forge source card now, combat selection next), defined once and tuned here, never per-screen.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (HighlightFx): the widget grows in place by `scale` (pure canvas transform — its layout size never changes, nothing around it moves) while a thick `outline_color` outline of `outline_width` px hugs its true composited silhouette, wrapped in a dense outer glow reaching `glow_span` px past the outline; `glow_spread` shapes the glow's density (higher = packed near the outline) and `glow_intensity` its brightness. Rides the composited-silhouette overlay path, so it never clips and never covers a badge or pip.

original.concept: THE 'this is interactive, and it is listening' cue for any card the player can actually press — on the board and in the hand alike. The card eases out of its row the way you ease one card proud of a real hand before deciding to play it.
original.explanation: NUMBERS ONLY — nothing plays this entry, CardUI READS it (see _set_hovered). Playing or attaching it does nothing. `rise` is the travel as a fraction of the card's OWN height, so it reads the same on a big hand card and a small tray one. `rise_secs`/`fall_secs` are the durations — fall a little slower than rise, so leaving settles rather than drops. THE EASING IS NOT A KNOB and lives in code on purpose: it is ease-in-out, which starts and ends at zero velocity. An ease-out here puts peak velocity on the first frame, which promises a much longer journey than the card actually makes and reads as a violent pop — that was the first version, and it is the one thing here that is a correctness call rather than taste.

original.concept: THE one answer to 'the pointer is on this' — for ANY widget, anywhere: a board unit, an empty slot, an ability, a hand card, the unit a turn-order entry is pointing at. One language, so the player learns 'yellow ring = the thing I am addressing' exactly once. Deliberately QUIETER than a selection: hover is a question, not a commitment.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (HoverFx + HighlightFx): a thick yellow outline hugging the widget's true composited silhouette and nothing else — no grow, no glow (glow_intensity 0). It OWNS the outline channel while it lives: a selected widget's white outline is muted for the duration while its glow keeps radiating, so the yellow ring reads on top with the white light around it.

original.concept: The card-details panel arriving beside the card it describes. At full size on frame one it reads as a second window opening, and the eye has to find it and then work out what it belongs to. Growing it OUT OF the card answers that before it is asked — the motion itself is the line drawn between the panel and its subject.
original.explanation: IMPLEMENTED (TooltipGrowFx): the panel scales 0 → 1 about its CORNER nearest the card, fading up over the first 70% of the span. THE CORNER IS THE WHOLE EFFECT — scaling about a corner leaves a whole QUADRANT of the panel at rest, and the eye locks onto that stationary region and watches the rest unfold away from it in one direction. Two rejected alternatives, both tried: the CENTRE grows every way at once and says nothing about where the panel came from; the truly-nearest POINT on the panel's edge is more literal but leaves only that one point still, so the panel flees it in opposite directions (top and bottom edges ~200px apart in 60ms) — an explosion, not an arrival. A corner only tells the truth when the card is DIAGONAL to the panel, which is why CardHoverPanel sits the panel off one of the card's corners (upper-right, then clockwise); placed beside and centred, the two facing corners are equidistant and a rounding error picks one. There is no exit half: the panel is dismissed by the pointer leaving, which has already happened by the time anything could play, so it simply goes.
original.prompt: Sprite sheet of an information panel unfolding upward and to the right out of its bottom-left corner, quick expand, 6 frames on transparent background, 2d game effect
